title: Secret loading and request signing in a ledger API
name: Ledger API secrets

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code loads, holds, compares or logs its secrets? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
What does LogStartup write for the config and signing_key attributes?
choices: The database URL and the signing key in clear text, since slog prints struct fields
Only the field names, because slog skips unexported fields
[redacted] for each secret, because Secret implements fmt, JSON and slog.LogValuer behaviour that hides the value
The key as a hex string, since []byte values are hex encoded by slog

questions.prompt: Why does the middleware compare signatures with hmac.Equal instead of bytes.Equal or ==?
choices: bytes.Equal would not compile for byte slices
hmac.Equal takes the same time whatever the position of the first differing byte, so response timing cannot be used to guess the signature byte by byte
hmac.Equal also hashes the body again to verify it

questions.prompt: A secret file with mode 0644 is mounted for LEDGER_SIGNING_KEY_FILE. What happens at startup?
choices: LoadConfig returns an error wrapping ErrInsecurePermissions, so the service does not start with that secret
The secret is loaded and a warning is logged
The file is read and then its mode is changed to 0600
Loading falls back to the LEDGER_SIGNING_KEY environment variable silently
